title: CDS Practice Set 13
pageDesc: Free CDS practice paper set 13 with detailed solutions. Pattern: English.

blueprint.name: English
blueprint.source: CDS Paper I English: 120 questions, 100 marks, 2 hours; negative 1/3.

questions.text: Improve the underlined segment. If no improvement is required, select 'No improvement'. **If he would have reached the station on time, he would have caught the train.**
questions.solution: Shortcut: Third Conditional (unreal past) requires 'If + Past Perfect (had + V3), ... would have + V3'. Eliminate options with 'would have' in 'If' clause (B) or Present Perfect (C). Worked: The sentence describes a past hypothetical condition. The correct structure is 'If he had reached... he would have caught'. Option A provides the necessary Past Perfect tense.

questions.text: Choose the word which best expresses the meaning: 'A person who collects coins as a hobby.'
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate using root words. 'Phil-' (love/stamps), 'Biblio-' (books), 'Carto-' (maps). 'Numismat-' relates to currency/coins. Worked: A Philatelist collects stamps; a Bibliophile loves books; a Cartographer draws maps. A Numismatist specifically collects or studies coins and medals.

questions.text: Improve the underlined segment in the sentence. If no improvement is required, select 'No improvement'. **I wish I was** a bird so that I could fly to you.
questions.solution: Elimination shortcut: The sentence expresses an **unreal/impossible wish** (Subjunctive Mood). In the Subjunctive Mood, the verb 'to be' always takes **'were'** for all persons (I, he, she, it, we, they). Option A uses 'were'. Option B ('am') is present indicative. Option C ('have been') is present perfect indicative. Option D is incorrect because 'was' is indicative past, not subjunctive.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect narration: He said, "Alas! I am undone."

options.label: A
options.text: He said that alas he was undone.

options.label: B
options.text: He exclaimed sadly that he was undone.

options.label: C
options.text: He exclaimed that alas he is undone.

options.label: D
options.text: He said sadly that he is undone.

questions.solution: Shortcut: For exclamatory sentences expressing sorrow ('Alas'), the reporting verb changes to 'exclaimed sadly/sorrowfully', the interjection 'Alas' is removed, conjunction 'that' is added, and the pronoun/tense shift occurs (I -> he, am -> was). Eliminate A and C (retain 'Alas'), and D (wrong reporting verb 'said' and tense 'is'). Option B applies all rules correctly.

rows: exclaimed sadly that he was undone

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error: Neither of the two candidates have submitted their nominations for the post.
questions.solution: Elimination shortcut: 'Neither of' is always followed by a plural noun/pronoun but takes a **singular verb**. Option A ('Neither of the two candidates') is the standard structure. Option C ('their nominations') correctly uses plural pronoun 'their' with plural noun 'nominations' (modern usage accepts 'their' for singular antecedent 'neither' to avoid gendered 'his/her'). Option D is a correct prepositional phrase. Option B uses plural verb 'have' with singular subject 'Neither'; it must be 'has submitted'.

questions.text: Choose the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank: The Board of Directors decided to ______ the services of the inefficient manager.
questions.solution: Elimination shortcut: 'Dispense' meaning 'to do without' or 'get rid of' **always** takes the preposition **'with'**. Options B, C, and D use incorrect prepositions ('of', 'off', 'away') which do not collocate with 'dispense' in standard English. 'Dispense with' means to abolish or stop using something/someone.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect narration: **He said to his friends, "Let us go out for a dinner tonight."**

options.label: A
options.text: He ordered his friends to go out for a dinner that night.

options.label: B
options.text: He requested his friends that let them go out for a dinner tonight.

options.label: C
options.text: He proposed his friends that they might go out for a dinner that night.

options.label: D
options.text: He suggested to his friends that they should go out for a dinner that night.

questions.solution: Shortcut: 'Let us' = Suggestion/Proposal. Reporting verb: 'suggested/proposed'. Structure: Subject + suggested + to + Object + that + Subject + should + V1. Eliminate 'ordered' (A), incorrect 'requested... let' structure (C), 'proposed... might' without 'to' (D). Worked: 'Let us' indicates a joint proposal. Indirect speech uses 'suggested to' + 'that they should go'. Option D follows the standard conversion rule.

rows: Suggested/Proposed + to + Obj + that + Sub + should + V1

questions.text: Choose the correct passive voice of the sentence: **'The committee will have approved the proposal by next week.'**

options.label: A
options.text: The proposal will be approved by the committee by next week.

options.label: B
options.text: The proposal would have been approved by the committee by next week.

options.label: C
options.text: The proposal will have been approved by the committee by next week.

options.label: D
options.text: The proposal is being approved by the committee by next week.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Future Perfect Active (will have + V3) becomes Passive: will have been + V3. Eliminate Simple Future (A), Modal 'would' (B), Present Continuous (D). Worked: Object 'The proposal' becomes subject. Auxiliary 'will have been' + Past Participle 'approved' + 'by the committee'. Option C matches this rule exactly.

questions.text: Choose the correct passive voice of the sentence: 'They have been building the bridge for two years.'

options.label: A
options.text: The bridge has been being built for two years.

options.label: B
options.text: The bridge is being built for two years.

options.label: C
options.text: The bridge has been built for two years.

options.label: D
options.text: The bridge was being built for two years.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the tense (Present Perfect Continuous: has/have + been + V-ing). The passive formula for this tense is Object + has/have + been + being + V3. Eliminate options B (Present Continuous), C (Present Perfect Simple), and D (Past Continuous). Only option A follows the 'has been being built' structure.

questions.text: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: **'To bite the bullet'**

options.label: B
options.text: To endure a painful situation bravely

questions.solution: Shortcut: Idioms are figurative; eliminate literal meanings (A, C). Historical context: soldiers bit bullets during surgery before anesthesia. Worked: The idiom means to force oneself to perform a painful or difficult task. Option B captures the sense of courageous endurance.

questions.text: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: **To burn the midnight oil**

options.label: A
options.text: To work late into the night

options.label: C
options.text: To light a lamp at midnight

options.label: D
options.text: To stay awake due to worry

questions.solution: Elimination shortcut: This is a standard idiom referencing the era before electric lights when oil lamps were used for studying/working at night. Option C is the literal meaning (trap). Option B implies negativity not inherent in the idiom. Option D specifies 'worry', whereas the idiom implies 'hard work/study' generally. Option A captures the correct figurative meaning of diligent late-night work.

questions.text: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To cry wolf'.
questions.solution: Shortcut: This idiom originates from Aesop's fable 'The Boy Who Cried Wolf', where a shepherd boy repeatedly tricks villagers into thinking a wolf is attacking. When a real wolf appears, no one believes him. The core meaning is 'raising a false alarm'. Eliminate literal interpretations (A, B) and unrelated meanings (D). Option C captures the exact essence.

questions.text: Select the one-word substitution for: 'A person who is indifferent to pleasure or pain.'
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use root/etymology elimination. 'Stoic' derives from Stoicism (endurance, indifference to pleasure/pain). 'Cynic' distrusts motives (Greek 'kynikos' - dog-like). 'Egoist' focuses on self-interest. 'Altruist' focuses on others' welfare. The definition 'indifferent to pleasure or pain' maps exclusively to Stoic.

questions.text: Select the word which is the **antonym** of the given word: **ABROGATE**
questions.solution: Elimination shortcut: 'Abrogate' means to repeal or abolish a law/formal agreement. Options A (Repeal), C (Abolish), and D (Annul) are all **synonyms**. In an antonym question, if three options share the same meaning, they must all be incorrect. Option B 'Enact' means to make a law/legislation, which is the direct opposite action.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: 'He is completely indifferent ______ the outcome of the election.'
questions.solution: Shortcut: The adjective 'indifferent' (meaning unconcerned/uninterested) is standardly followed by the preposition 'to'. Eliminate 'for' (used with 'eligible/qualified'), 'with' (used with 'angry/pleased'), and 'at' (used with 'surprised/angry' - specific target). Only 'to' forms the correct collocation.
